questions.questionText: Which of the following is a pure public goods?
questions.questionTextEn: Which of the following is a pure public goods?
questions.explanation: A purely public or social goods is one whose production creates external benefits and such benefits are used by many individuals, which are arranged by the budget, and whose consumption by one person does not reduce the availability of that item for other people living in the society. These goods are supplied equally to all persons. In the context of pure public goods, the market system (Price system), the principle of rivalry and exclusion does not apply. National security is a pure public goods, infrastructure (road, rail, bridge, etc.) is public goods and education, health, mid-day meal, housing available with financial assistance are merit goods.
